questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Be alert to oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less grip than dry pavement.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Weave between lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be more visible at intersections. Ride in a lane position that gives you a clear view of oncoming traffic. Keep space around your bike so you can move safely if needed.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks still in the body.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not speed up this process. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you more visible in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on your body.
There is an effect, but it only lasts a short time.
There is an effect, but coffee can eliminate it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding skills. Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Coffee does not speed up this process.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: It improves your view of the road ahead.
It reduces your view of the road ahead.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It improves your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass improves your view and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride?

options.text: As close to the shoulder as possible.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. This position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: How can you lower your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride where it is hard to be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your bike.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up and skidding during hard braking. It works when you press both brake controls hard. When sensors detect a wheel might lock, the system releases and re-applies the brakes to keep braking power at its best.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs:

options.text: Only a mechanic to do checks.

questions.correctAnswerText: More attention.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent problems. Small issues on a motorcycle can be more serious than on a car.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Expect it to handle like your own bike.
Assume the owner checked the brakes.
Keep extra distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep extra distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and leave extra space for stopping.

questions.question: How does a passenger affect motorcycle riding?

options.text: It usually doesn't change how the bike handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It helps new riders learn different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight that changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as without a passenger.
Only put footrests out for yourself.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have the right equipment for a passenger. It needs a separate seat, footrests for the passenger, and may need adjustments to the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go slower.
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden movements can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: What should riders know about motorcycle blind spots in traffic?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to cause problems.
Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before you ride. Press each one fully and make sure it feels firm and stops the motorcycle.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect like:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: A rectangular road sign is usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: A speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other traffic rules are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You should honk to make the driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always pass only where it is safe and legal. You must start and finish your pass within a passing zone.
